Planning Group Transportation for Weddings: Complete Guest Logistics Guide

Short answer: count the guests staying at your hotel block, book enough seats to move them in one trip, and run the vehicles for the whole evening so nobody is stranded. For most Scottsdale weddings that is one or two Executive Mini Coaches for 6 to 8 hours, which works out to about $47 to $54 per seat before tax. Everything below shows you how to get there.

Guest transportation can make or break the day, not just for you but for everyone attending. Here is how Scottsdale Sprinters plans it with couples every weekend.

Why guest transportation matters

Parking. Desert venues and resort ballrooms rarely have enough spots. Guests circling the lot miss the processional, and valet adds cost and a line at the end of the night.

Drinking responsibly. An open bar plus a drive home is a liability for you and a risk for them. A shuttle removes the question. Guests 21 and over can even bring a drink aboard for the ride back to the hotel: Arizona's open-container law, A.R.S. § 4-251, exempts passengers in a vehicle for hire. No one under 21 drinks and the driver never does. Read the full explainer.

Remote venues. Cave Creek, Fountain Hills and north Scottsdale addresses confuse GPS at dusk. One professional driver who has been there beats 40 phones guessing.

The experience. Guests arrive together, excited, on time. They leave together, safely. That is the difference between a wedding and a logistics problem.

Assessing your transportation needs

Step 1: Evaluate the venue

  • How many parking spots are actually available?
  • Is there valet, and what does it cost your guests?
  • How far is the nearest hotel block?
  • Is the road in paved, lit and easy to find at night?
  • Where can a 29-seat bus load without blocking the entrance?

Step 2: Count out-of-town guests

Almost everyone in this group needs a ride: they flew in, did not rent a car, do not know the roads and plan to enjoy the bar.

Step 3: Count local guests who want the shuttle

Locals ride when parking is tight, when they want to drink, or when the venue is far. Ask on the RSVP card. Expect roughly a third to half of locals to say yes if you offer it.

Step 4: Total it

Out-of-town + local shuttle riders = seats you need to move at the peak, which is almost always the hotel-to-ceremony run.

One big shuttle vs. two smaller ones. One Executive Mini Coach moves everyone at once from a single hotel. Two Executive Sprinters cover two hotels or staggered departures, but you pay two minimums. For a single hotel block, one bus almost always wins.

Worked examples (per seat, real rates)

Per-seat cost is the vehicle fare divided by its seats, rounded to the dollar, before tax. Multi-vehicle totals are simply the fare times the number of vehicles.

60 guests, one hotel, ceremony and reception at the same venue

  • Two Executive Mini Coaches (58 seats) for 6 hours: $1,350 each, $2,700 total plus 8% tax.
  • Each bus is about $47 per seat.
  • Timeline: hotel pickup 3:00 PM, ceremony 4:00 PM, buses stand by, departures at 9:30 and 11:00 PM.

85 guests at two hotels, 8-hour evening

  • Three Executive Mini Coaches (87 seats), 8 hours requested, 7 billed with the free hour: $1,575 each, $4,725 total plus 8% tax.
  • About $54 per seat.
  • Two buses start at the main hotel block; the third starts at the second hotel. All three run the loop back at the end of the night.

100 guests, one hotel, party crowd

  • The 56-Passenger Motorcoach and the Party Bus (28 Pax) carry 84 in one movement. Eight hours bills 7: the motorcoach is $2,275, or $2,457 with tax, about $41 a seat; the party bus is $1,750, or $1,890 with tax, about $62.50 a seat.
  • This is the pair rather than three of anything. From a single hotel both run a second loop for the rest of the list, and the party bus makes the ride home part of the party.

Add the wedding party

  • Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) for 8 hours (billed 7): $1,225, or $1,323 with tax. About $77 per seat for a 16-person bridal party from getting-ready suite to first look to ceremony to reception, with the vehicle standing by for photos.
  • For a 5-hour wedding-party-only booking: $875 ($945 with tax), about $55 per seat.

Budget guest shuttle

  • One Mini Bus (24 Pax) for 6 hours: $1,110, or $1,199 with tax. About $46 per seat for a smaller block. Minimal luggage.

Prices are quoted per vehicle, so add tax and you have the whole number. Nothing else is added.

How early to book

  • Peak-season Saturdays (October through April): availability varies by date. Vehicles with 24 or more seats are the largest in the fleet; request a current quote for your date and we will confirm in writing which of them is open.
  • Off-peak or weekday weddings: request a current quote for the date.
  • Big-event weekends (the WM Phoenix Open, Barrett-Jackson week, spring-training weekends): treat them like peak Saturdays and request a current quote when you sign the venue contract.
  • Under 30 days: call our reservations team. We can often help; read the cancellation terms below before you commit.

Book the guest shuttle right after the venue and the hotel block. Those three decisions depend on each other.

Creating your transportation timeline

Pre-ceremony shuttle

  • Depart the hotel 45 to 60 minutes before the ceremony
  • Allow 15 minutes for loading (people are never at the curb at the exact minute)
  • Build in buffer for traffic and the one guest looking for their room key
  • Arrive 15 minutes before the processional

Example for a 4:00 PM ceremony: 2:45 PM bus in the lobby driveway, 3:00 PM depart, 3:30 PM arrive at the venue.

Ceremony to reception (if different venues)

Load right after the receiving line, with a 15 to 20 minute buffer. Announce it before the recessional so nobody wanders.

Continuous service vs. scheduled runs

Continuous (recommended for one hotel): the bus loops hotel to venue to hotel all evening. Guests leave when they are ready. Best for receptions of 4 or more hours.

Scheduled runs: set departures (9:00, 10:30, midnight). Cheaper only if it lets you drop hours. Requires clear announcements.

End of night

  • Post the departure times in the program and on a sign at the exit
  • Have the DJ or emcee announce each one 15 minutes ahead
  • Final departure should leave 15 minutes after the reception ends, not at the minute it ends

Logistics details

Pickup locations

Hotel: confirm the loading area with the front desk, ask them to announce the shuttle in the lobby, and put a small sign on an easel.

Venue: designate one loading zone, ideally covered, and mark it. Tell the coordinator where the bus will stage.

Communicating with guests

Put the shuttle times on the wedding website, in the welcome bag and in a text the morning of. Be specific: "Main lobby driveway, 3:00 PM, returns at 9:30 and 11:00." Tell them what happens if they drive themselves.

Day-of coordination

Assign one person who is not in the wedding party to own the shuttle: confirm the driver's arrival, herd guests, relay delays, make the call on holding the last bus. A day-of coordinator is ideal. Give that person our reservations team's number.

Troubleshooting

"We have multiple hotels." One bus does a loop, or two smaller vehicles run staggered pickups. Or name one primary hotel and let the others meet there.

"Guests arrive on different days." Book the wedding-day shuttle only. Point everyone else to the airport options in our Sky Harbor guide.

"Our venue is hard to find." That is the strongest argument for a shuttle. Give self-drivers a pin, not an address.

"Guests want to leave at different times." Continuous service with two announced departures handles it. Rideshare is the backup for the stragglers.

Cancellation for weddings

Cancellation terms depend on your date and booking; read the cancellation policy before you book. You get one free date change when you ask 72 or more hours ahead. If we ever cancel, everything is refunded. Full wording is on the policies page.

Questions to ask any transportation company

  1. What exactly is included in the quoted price, and is tax in it?
  2. What is the minimum, and what does an extra hour cost?
  3. Is a tip added to my bill, or is it my choice?
  4. Can we see the actual vehicle we are booking?
  5. What is the backup plan if a vehicle has a problem?
  6. How many weddings do you run a month?
  7. Are you licensed and insured, and can you send a certificate?
  8. What is the cancellation policy in writing?
  9. Can the driver handle multiple pickup points on one run?
  10. Who do we call on the day?
